items.title: AI Vulnerability Finding
items.reason: Schneier's post mostly reproduces an unverified X claim that AI found ~3% of all critical bugs in history in one month; the one hard data point (Postgres backport commits up >60% YoY) is real but secondhand, and commenters dispute the headline figure.
key_facts: Quoted claim: AI could add ~26% to the all-time count of critical bugs found, this year alone — unverified
Robert Haas: PostgreSQL 19 delayed partly because AI makes bugs easier to find; back-patched commits up >60% YoY
Commenters split on whether this reflects new bug classes or just faster triage of known ones

items.title: Backporting security fixes at scale with Codex
items.reason: Trail of Bits built a working Codex-based pipeline that has already landed fixes for 149 CVEs into stable Linux kernels plus Fedora/Ubuntu packages — running code with hard numbers, exactly the kind of AI x cyber result the profile wants.
key_facts: 149 distinct CVEs backported into stable Linux kernel releases as of Oct 29
Simple backport ~30 min human attention, complex one ~3 hours, down from days
5.10.y alone had 2,006 unfixed kernel CVEs as of Sept 18; Debian 13 had 4,562 unique unfixed CVEs
Public tracker: trailofbits.github.io/ptp-linux-stable-cve-dashboard
